messages:
Maya R: observed ~18% drop in prefix cache hit rate after canary of system-prompt v2 + tokenizer 2.4. Deployed 2321122300. Rolling requests show more misses on short-prefix cohorts. Opening thread to correlate with kernel/batching changes.
Sam O: looking at profiler: miss spikes align with -> kernel switch to async-batched kernels at t+5m. KV lookup latency jump +6ms; hit-rate down for sequences <32 tokens.
Leo P: hmm could be key normalization mismatch — system prompt added a trailing newline and tool call metadata ordering changed. Did we canonicalize tool fields? :thinking: 
Anya K: we didn't. tool metadata is included in cache key as an unsorted JSON string. That explains churn when tool order changed across SDKs.
Maya R: ok hypothesis: tokenizer bump changed tokenization of the system prompt prefix and the tool order churn amplified mismatch. Can we simulate: normalize -> sort tool keys + strip trailing whitespace + pin tokenizer version in key.
Sam O: ran quick local experiment: normalizing tool fields (sort object keys) recovered ~12% hit rate in cohort A. Command:
```
# toy normalizer
def normalize(msg):
  msg['system'] = msg['system'].rstrip('\\n')
  msg['tools'] = sorted_keys(msg['tools'])
  return json.dumps(msg, separators=(',',':'))
```

Leo P: good. Also noticed kernel selection changes batch formation: the async kernel splits short sequences into micro-batches that don't reuse KV cache as effectively. We see more prefix eviction because of shorter per-batch sequence tails.
Anya K: possible mitigation: adjust batching heuristic to prefer grouping by prefix fingerprint when available — prioritize grouping same normalized-key in same batch for X ms window.
Sam O: micro-experiment: hold-batching-by-prefix for 30ms reduced miss rate another 4% but added median latency +8ms for single token requests.
Maya R: tradeoff. We need SLO-aware knob. Proposal: add opt-in routing policy 'prefix-affinity' for latency-tolerant routes, and default to strict-latency for interactive endpoints.
Anya K: also suggest fallback: if tokenizer version bump detected, create transient compatibility layer: compute both old and new key variants for a short warmup window.
Leo P: that's smart — dual-keying for 5 minutes after deploy reduces cold miss but doubles key lookups. cheap compared to perf cost.
deploy-bot: Deploy notice: canary v2.18 rolled at 2321122300 across 10% hosts.
Maya R: next steps: (1) add tool-field canonicalizer + whitespace strip PR, (2) prototype prefix-affinity batching hook, (3) experiment with dual-key warmup on next canary. I'll open issues and tag infra/scheduling.
Sam O: I'll attach profiler snippets and exact hit-rate graphs to the issue.
Leo P: ping me for batching heuristic PR review.
Anya K: I'll draft compatibility plan for tokenizer pinning and dual-key warmup.
Maya R: thanks everyone. If we can get a quick soft rollback option too in case miss rate worsens, please do.
Sam O: noted — rollback flag is ready.
Maya R: :thumbsup:
